summary.short: California statute giving consumers rights to know, delete, correct and opt out of the sale or sharing of their personal information, and to limit use of sensitive data and minors' data. Binds businesses above revenue or volume thresholds and their service providers. Enforced by the California Privacy Protection Agency and the Attorney General.
summary.long: Gives California consumers rights to know, delete, correct and opt out of sale or sharing of their personal information, and to limit use of sensitive personal information (§§1798.105–1798.121). Affirmative authorization is required before selling data of consumers under 16. Businesses must give notice at collection, provide request methods, and not discriminate against consumers exercising rights (§§1798.100, 1798.125, 1798.130, 1798.135). Duties apply to businesses doing business in California that meet revenue, volume or data-sale thresholds (§1798.140(d)); service providers and contractors must act under written contracts. Exemptions cover certain medical, credit, financial and deidentified data (§§1798.145–1798.146). Consumers may sue for statutory damages of USD 100 to 750 per incident after certain security breaches (§1798.150). The California Privacy Protection Agency enforces through administrative fines of up to USD 2,500 per violation, or 7,500 for intentional violations; the Attorney General may seek civil penalties (§§1798.155, 1798.199.90). The Agency's regulations cover opt-out signals, risk assessments, cybersecurity audits and automated decisionmaking (§1798.185). Local laws are preempted (§1798.180).

A sole proprietorship, partnership, limited liability company, corporation, association, or other legal entity that is organized or operated for the profit or financial benefit of its shareholders or other owners
“Consumer” means a natural person who is a California resident

“Personal information” means information that identifies, relates to, describes, is reasonably capable of being associated with, or could reasonably be linked, directly or indirectly, with a particular consumer or household
“Personal information” does not include publicly available information or lawfully obtained, truthful information that is a matter of public concern
“Deidentified” means information that cannot reasonably be used to infer information about, or otherwise be linked to, a particular consumer
“Aggregate consumer information” means information that relates to a group or category of consumers
“Sensitive personal information” means:
“Biometric information” means an individual’s physiological, biological, or behavioral characteristics
“Precise geolocation” means any data that is derived from a device
means buying, renting, gathering, obtaining, receiving, or accessing any personal information pertaining to a consumer by any means
means selling, renting, releasing, disclosing, disseminating, making available, transferring, or otherwise communicating orally, in writing, or by electronic or other means
“Share,” “shared,” or “sharing” means sharing, renting, releasing
“Cross-context behavioral advertising” means the targeting of advertising to a consumer based on the consumer’s personal information
“Service provider” means a person that processes personal information on behalf of a business
“Contractor” means a person to whom the business makes available a consumer’s personal information for a business purpose, pursuant to a written contract with the business
“Third party” means a person who is not any of the following
“Business purpose” means the use of personal information for the business’ operational purposes
“Household” means a group, however identified, of consumers who cohabitate with one another at the same residential address
“Consent” means any freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous indication of the consumer’s wishes
“Dark pattern” means a user interface designed or manipulated with the substantial effect of subverting or impairing user autonomy
“Profiling” means any form of automated processing of personal information
“Control” or “controlled” means ownership of, or the power to vote, more than 50 percent of the outstanding shares of any class of voting security of a business
“Verifiable consumer request” means a request that is made by a consumer

evidence.quote: shall be prohibited, pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (c) of Section 1798.135, from selling or sharing the consumer’s personal information after its receipt of the consumer’s direction

obligations.summary: May not sell or share personal information of consumers under 16 without affirmative authorization (consumer aged 13-15 or parent/guardian for under 13).
obligations.conditional_on: business has actual knowledge that the consumer is less than 16 years of age

evidence.quote: a business shall not sell or share the personal information of consumers if the business has actual knowledge that the consumer is less than 16 years of age

obligations.summary: Provide notice of use or disclosure of sensitive personal information for purposes beyond those listed, and of the right to limit it.
obligations.conditional_on: business uses or discloses sensitive personal information for purposes other than those in subdivision (a)

evidence.quote: shall provide notice to consumers, pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 1798.135

obligations.summary: After a direction to limit use of sensitive personal information, may not use or disclose it for other purposes unless the consumer consents.
obligations.conditional_on: consumer has directed the business to limit use of sensitive personal information

evidence.quote: shall be prohibited, pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (c) of Section 1798.135, from using or disclosing the consumer’s sensitive personal information

obligations.summary: May not discriminate against a consumer for exercising rights, including by denying goods or services, charging different prices, or providing different quality.

evidence.quote: A business shall not discriminate against a consumer because the consumer exercised any of the consumer’s rights under this title

obligations.summary: Notify consumers of financial incentives offered under subdivision (b) pursuant to Section 1798.130.
obligations.conditional_on: business offers financial incentives

evidence.quote: shall notify consumers of the financial incentives pursuant to Section 1798.130

obligations.summary: Enter a consumer into a financial incentive program only with prior opt-in consent describing material terms; wait at least 12 months before re-requesting after refusal.
obligations.conditional_on: business offers a financial incentive program

evidence.quote: A business may enter a consumer into a financial incentive program only if the consumer gives the business prior opt-in consent

obligations.summary: May not use financial incentive practices that are unjust, unreasonable, coercive, or usurious.

evidence.quote: A business shall not use financial incentive practices that are unjust, unreasonable, coercive, or usurious in nature.

obligations.summary: Make available two or more designated request methods, including at minimum a toll-free number (email only for exclusively online businesses with direct relationships), and the website where applicable.

evidence.quote: Make available to consumers two or more designated methods for submitting requests

obligations.summary: Disclose and deliver required information free of charge, correct or delete data on request, within 45 days of a verifiable request (one 45-day extension with notice); information in readily useable format; authentication may be required.
obligations.conditional_on: verifiable consumer request

evidence.quote: Disclose and deliver the required information to a consumer free of charge

obligations.summary: Disclose consumer rights, request methods, categories collected, sources, purposes, third-party disclosures and sale/sharing lists in its online privacy policy, updated at least every 12 months.

evidence.quote: Disclose the following information in its online privacy policy or policies

obligations.summary: Ensure individuals handling consumer inquiries are informed of the requirements of the title and how to direct consumers to exercise their rights.

evidence.quote: Ensure that all individuals responsible for handling consumer inquiries

obligations.summary: Use personal information collected for request verification solely for verification, without further disclosure, unnecessary retention or unrelated use.

evidence.quote: Use any personal information collected from the consumer in connection with the business’ verification

obligations.summary: Provide a clear and conspicuous homepage link to opt out of sale or sharing and a link to limit use of sensitive personal information, or a single combined link.
obligations.conditional_on: business sells or shares personal information, or uses sensitive personal information beyond permitted purposes

evidence.quote: Provide a clear and conspicuous link on the business’ internet homepages

obligations.summary: May not require a consumer to create an account or provide additional information beyond what is necessary to exercise opt-out or limit choices.
obligations.conditional_on: business is subject to subdivision (a) or (b) of Section 1798.135

evidence.quote: Not require a consumer to create an account or provide additional information

obligations.summary: After an opt-out or limit request, refrain from selling or sharing the personal information or using sensitive personal information, and wait at least 12 months before re-requesting consent.
obligations.conditional_on: consumer has exercised the right to opt out or limit

evidence.quote: refrain from selling or sharing the consumer’s personal information

obligations.summary: For consumers under 16 who do not consent, refrain from selling or sharing their personal information and wait at least 12 months before requesting consent again, unless authorized by regulations or the consumer turns 16.
obligations.conditional_on: consumer under 16 years of age who does not consent

evidence.quote: refrain from selling or sharing the personal information of the consumer under 16 years of age

obligations.summary: A person to whom an opt-out request is communicated may use the consumer's information only for the specified business purpose and may not sell, share, retain, use or disclose it outside the permitted purposes.
obligations.conditional_on: business communicates an opt-out request to a person authorized to collect personal information

evidence.quote: the person shall thereafter only use that consumer’s personal information for a business purpose specified by the business

obligations.summary: Inform the consumer of any extension of the response period within 45 days of receipt, with reasons; inform the consumer of reasons for not taking action and any right to appeal.
obligations.conditional_on: response extended, or business does not act on a request

evidence.quote: The business shall inform the consumer of any such extension within 45 days of receipt of the request, together with the reasons for the delay.

obligations.summary: May not reidentify, or attempt to reidentify, deidentified patient information, except for listed purposes.
obligations.conditional_on: information met the deidentification requirements of Section 1798.146(a)(4)

evidence.quote: A business or other person shall not reidentify, or attempt to reidentify, information

obligations.summary: Contracts for sale or license of deidentified patient information must include statements that the information is deidentified patient information, that reidentification is prohibited, and onward-disclosure limits.
obligations.conditional_on: one party is a person residing or doing business in the state

evidence.quote: Beginning January 1, 2021, any contract for the sale or license of deidentified information

obligations.summary: Consumer Privacy Fund monies are to be used exclusively for listed purposes, including court, agency and Attorney General costs and grants.

evidence.quote: Funds transferred to the Consumer Privacy Fund shall be used exclusively as follows:

obligations.summary: Attorney General must solicit public participation and adopt regulations furthering the title, including the listed areas (categories, exceptions, opt-out rules, verification, and others).

evidence.quote: the Attorney General shall solicit broad public participation and adopt regulations to further the purposes of this title

obligations.summary: Regulations are to require businesses whose processing presents significant risk to submit regular risk assessments to the California Privacy Protection Agency, weighing benefits against risks.
obligations.conditional_on: regulations adopted under 1798.185(a)(14) for processing presenting significant risk

evidence.quote: Submit to the California Privacy Protection Agency on a regular basis a risk assessment with respect to their processing of personal information

obligations.summary: Regulations are to require annual cybersecurity audits by businesses whose processing presents significant risk to security.
obligations.conditional_on: regulations adopted under 1798.185(a)(14) for processing presenting significant risk

evidence.quote: Perform a cybersecurity audit on an annual basis

obligations.summary: Regulations are to govern access and opt-out rights concerning business use of automated decisionmaking technology, including profiling, and meaningful information about the logic involved.

evidence.quote: Issuing regulations governing access and opt-out rights with respect to a business’ use of automated decisionmaking technology

obligations.summary: Establishes the California Privacy Protection Agency, a five-member board, with full administrative power to implement and enforce the title.

evidence.quote: There is hereby established in state government the California Privacy Protection Agency

obligations.summary: Agency is to adopt, amend and rescind regulations under Section 1798.185, including regulations specifying recordkeeping requirements for businesses.
obligations.applies_from: On and after the later of July 1, 2021, or within six months of the agency providing the Attorney General with notice that it is prepared to assume rulemaking responsibilities

evidence.quote: adopt, amend, and rescind regulations pursuant to Section 1798.185 to carry out the purposes and provisions

obligations.summary: Agency is to provide a public report summarizing the risk assessments filed with it, without compromising data security.

evidence.quote: provide a public report summarizing the risk assessments filed with the agency

obligations.summary: Agency is to appoint a Chief Privacy Auditor to conduct audits of businesses to ensure compliance.

evidence.quote: appoint a Chief Privacy Auditor to conduct audits of businesses to ensure compliance with this title

obligations.summary: Agency is to adjust the monetary thresholds in the listed provisions to reflect CPI increases.
obligations.applies_from: On January 1, 2025, and on January 1 of any odd-numbered year thereafter

evidence.quote: the California Privacy Protection Agency shall adjust the monetary thresholds

obligations.summary: Agency is to post the adjusted monetary thresholds on its website.
obligations.applies_from: No later than January 15 of the year in which the adjustment becomes effective

evidence.quote: The agency shall post the adjusted monetary thresholds on its internet website no later than January 15

enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of this title by any business, service provider, contractor, or other person, in an administrative enforcement action brought by the California Privacy Protection Agency
enforcement.max_penalty_text: not more than two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) for each violation or seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500) for each intentional violation or violations involving the personal information of consumers whom the business, service provider, contractor, or other person has actual knowledge are under 16 years of age, as adjusted pursuant to subdivision (d) of Section 1798.199.95
enforcement.penalty_formula: Per violation: $2,500; $7,500 per intentional violation or violation involving personal information of consumers the business has actual knowledge are under 16; amounts adjusted under Section 1798.199.95(d)
enforcement.cure_period: No fixed period stated; the agency may decline to investigate or provide time to cure (Section 1798.199.45(a)) and must consider good faith cooperation (Section 1798.199.100)

evidence.quote: shall be liable for an administrative fine of not more than two thousand five hundred dollars

enforcement.triggered_by: Agency determination after a hearing that a violation of this title has occurred
enforcement.max_penalty_text: order may require the violator to cease and desist violation of this title
enforcement.cure_period: Agency may decide to provide a time period to cure the alleged violation (Section 1798.199.45(a))

evidence.quote: Cease and desist violation of this title.

enforcement.authority: Attorney General (civil action in the name of the people of the State of California)
enforcement.triggered_by: Violation of this title, recovered in a civil action brought by the Attorney General; no such action may be filed after the agency has issued a decision or order against the same person for the same violation (Section 1798.199.90(d))
enforcement.max_penalty_text: civil penalty of not more than two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) for each violation or seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500) for each intentional violation and each violation involving the personal information of minor consumers, as adjusted pursuant subdivision (d) of Section 1798.199.95
enforcement.penalty_formula: Per violation: $2,500; $7,500 per intentional violation and per violation involving personal information of minor consumers; court may consider good faith cooperation; injunction also available

evidence.quote: liable for a civil penalty of not more than two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) for each violation

enforcement.triggered_by: Unauthorized access and exfiltration, theft, or disclosure of nonencrypted and nonredacted personal information as a result of the business's violation of the duty to implement and maintain reasonable security procedures
enforcement.max_penalty_text: not less than one hundred dollars ($100) and not greater than seven hundred and fifty ($750) per consumer per incident or actual damages, whichever is greater; amounts adjusted pursuant to subdivision (d) of Section 1798.199.95
enforcement.penalty_formula: $100 to $750 per consumer per incident, or actual damages, whichever is greater; injunctive or declaratory relief and other relief the court deems proper also available
enforcement.cure_period: Consumer must give the business 30 days' written notice before an action for statutory damages; a cure is possible if the business cures within the 30 days and gives an express written statement (Section 1798.150(b))

evidence.quote: To recover damages in an amount not less than one hundred dollars ($100) and not greater than seven hundred and fifty ($750) per consumer per incident or actual damages, whichever is greater.
